title: Typing E. coli ATCC 11303 with fluorescently stained virus
author: Dr. Steven Wilhelm
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iivcce6

steps.title: Prepare E. coli Culture
steps.instruction: Grow a 4 hour culture of ATCC 11303 in Fe-free LB by inoculating ATCC 11303 from an overnight culture grown in Fe-Free media into fresh media.

steps.title: Stain Cells with Virus
steps.instruction: Prepare the stained culture in a sterile 1.5 mL tube.

substeps.instruction: Add the 4 hour ATCC 11303 culture into a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Allow culture to sit in the dark at room temperature for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Cells for Filtration
steps.instruction: Process the culture to concentrate the cells and adjust the buffer.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the cells at ~10,000 rpm for 3 minutes.
Gently remove the supernatant with a pipette.
Re-suspend the bacterial pellet in 1.5 ml of 10 mM MgSO4.

steps.title: Filter and Rinse Sample
steps.instruction: Filter the sample and clean the filter membrane.

substeps.instruction: Filter the sample onto a 0.2 μm pore-size, black polycarbonate filter.
Rinse the filter gently three times with 1 ml of 10 mM MgSO4.

steps.title: Mount Filter for Imaging
steps.instruction: Mount the filter onto a glass slide using glycerol or immersion oil.

substeps.instruction: Pipet a drop of glycerol or immersion oil in the middle of a clean glass slide and place a cover glass on top.
Let the glycerol spread evenly under the cover glass and remove any bubbles.
Remove the cover slip from the slide, place the filter on the slide, and replace the cover slip.
